title: Authentication Ticket Store: Keep Sign-In Tickets on the Server | Orchard Core
description:
By default, the authentication ticket of a signed-in user lives in a cookie. A user with many roles and permissions gets a large cookie, and a large cookie can push requests over the header limit.

The Users Authentication Ticket Store feature keeps the tickets on the server, in a memory cache or in Redis, and leaves the browser with a session identifier. This video shows where the feature is, what its code does, and how to share the tickets between several instances of a site.

In this video:
• Why a ticket store: large cookies, and the server-side answer
• Enable the feature: Tools, Features, and the Feature recipe step
• How it works: the session store, and the code that stores, retrieves, removes and renews a ticket
• Where the tickets live: the memory cache, Redis, and shared Data Protection keys
